A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PFAAs are used in specialty and functional textiles, and that PFAA levels are higher in flame-retardant textiles than in water-repellent or infant clothes.
the use of PFAAs in textiles is still prevalent in the United States.

PFAA precursor concentrations were higher in flame retardant and water repellent textiles than in infant clothes, but PFAAs in textiles are not expected to pose significant health risk to the general public.

the total oxidizable precursor assay is an effective method for the determination of PFAAs in textiles.
the oxidative treatment should be considered in the analysis of textile samples to better assess the presence of precursors of PFAAs.
